finding: Two of the four mechanisms are real and measured, and two are absent. The state names are adopted rather than invented and the terminal ones are distinguished and acted on differently - the same document reaches rejected under a ceiling it cannot meet and cancelled under a mid-flight cancel that actually stopped the turn after 3 frames with a tool call refused, not merely recorded. But none of that is reachable through the intake door: the acknowledgement carries entry id, correlation id, job digest and accepted and no task handle or state, the surface serves zero cancel or subscribe operations, and the example's own README says so. Correlation and idempotency are first-class members of the local envelope rather than declared extension attributes of the published envelope - on the wire they leave as bespoke HTTP headers with the whole envelope nested inside the event's data member, which is where an intermediary cannot read them - and exactly one content mode is ever handled, with no binary-mode header anywhere.
gap: A subscription or streaming path and a cancellation operation published on the intake door itself, with a handle in the acknowledgement a detached producer can use, since the detached binding is the one case those mechanisms exist for; correlation and idempotency carried as named extension attributes on the published envelope instead of custom headers plus a nested payload; and deliberate handling of both content modes, including a binary-mode arrival, rather than the structured one alone.

finding: The external door is a registered producer format whose native message carries the agent-messaging shape, mapped by a declared mapper rather than by a per-caller payload, so none of the three errors the direction names is being committed - there is no bespoke payload per door, no door's wire format became the internal shape, and no caller has to adopt code from this side. But nothing about the revision is on the wire: zero protocol-version or capability-card fields exist anywhere under the intake surface, no revision is served and none is refused, and the versions are declared only in README prose and marked unverified because no specification page has ever been fetched here. The one binding that can reach a real route refuses to invent the protocol's own method name and requires the operator to supply it, which is honest and is also the measure of how little of the specification is actually held. No listener is served at all, so no outside caller has integrated and none could.
gap: A served external door that states its protocol revision on the wire and refuses an unsupported one explicitly with a typed problem, a fetched specification behind the version strings so they stop being unverified prose, and a recorded integration by a caller who wrote nothing from this side - today the door exists only as a message shape a local mapper reads, with the method name deferred to the operator.
